title: Intake sampler + readiness trajectory for Private/VPC/on‑prem requests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: As we scale Private/VPC/on‑prem requests we need a faster, more deterministic way to prioritize and route non-bug customer asks (networking, upgrades, air‑gapped constraints). Current intake is freeform and often requires multiple manual touchpoints to surface real blockers (firewalls, proxy requirements, OS constraints, upgrade runway).

Goal: Build an "intake sampler" and readiness-trajectory model that classifies requests into concise lanes (fast-track, engineering-led, remediation-required) with an explicable score and recommended minimal next steps. This should reduce TTR (time-to-response) for triage teams and give sales/CS clarity on delivery timelines.

Core ideas: trajectory score (0-100) representing estimated engineering effort in story points and likely calendar runway; compatibility sieve that tags required network primitives (outbound HTTPS, gRPC, DNS whitelisting, proxy), and a manifest template customers fill to auto-populate the estimator. Provide clear communications templates per lane (fast-track acceptance, risk notice, remediation plan).

Non-goals: This ticket excludes implementation of the deployment itself or low-level kernel/runtime changes. It focuses on intake heuristics, scoring calibration, and communications + minimal automation for routing to the right internal lane.
acceptance_criteria: A lightweight intake form is defined (fields + examples) and validated with Solutions Engineering and Sales reps
Trajectory scoring algorithm doc describing inputs, weights, and edge cases is published in Confluence
Prototype compatibility sieve that maps intake fields to one of three lanes (fast-track, engineering review, remediation required) exists and can be run as a spreadsheet or simple script
Comms templates (email/slack) for each lane are created and approved by PM and Legal
Dashboard wireframe showing counts by lane, average trajectory score, and mean time to triage is created and reviewed by Console PM
Pilot run with 10 incoming customer requests demonstrates faster initial triage (target: reduce manual back-and-forth by >= 40%)
implementation_notes: Intake form minimal required fields: customer name, deployment type (VPC/on‑prem/airgapped), OS and orchestration, outbound network constraints, proxy allowed (Y/N), maintenance window restrictions, current runtime version, desired go‑live date, contact for network ops

Suggested scoring weights (initial): outbound connectivity restrictions 30%, proxy disallowed 25%, kernel/runtime version mismatch 20%, maintenance window tightness 10%, custom HW/OS requirements 10%, compliance-required integrations 5%
Define mapping table: if proxy_disallowed + outbound_restrictions -> lane=remediation_required; if proxy_allowed and only DNS/port whitelisting -> lane=fast-track; else lane=engineering_review
Telemetry hooks: record intake fields into a triage dataset (BigQuery table), capture pre/post triage timestamps for MTTR calculation
Cross-team owners: PM (Aisha) owns spec + comms, Solutions Eng (TBD) owns intake validation, Eng infra (ENG-4123) owns any automation to accept manifests, Legal to sign off on comm templates

Artifact links: initial spec draft in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PD/pages/INTAKE-TRAJECTORY (placeholder), sample manifest template in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/priv-deploy/manifest-sample.xlsx
Pilot plan: run with 10 inbound customer leads flagged by Sales over 3 weeks; collect feedback from SE and CS on missing fields and false positives
